block_05_direct_answer.title: Direct answer
block_05_direct_answer.body_html: Projects should be compared using the same decision criteria across both options. For luxury buyers, compare developer strength, location, unit layout, total price, payment plan, project stage, handover, service costs and buyer or investment fit. Use the same assumptions across options and focus on material differences rather than marketing claims.

items.answer: Projects should be compared using the same decision criteria across both options. For luxury buyers, compare similar unit types, usable area, included features and payment timing rather than treating headline starting prices as directly comparable.
items.question: How do I compare projects?

items.answer: Choosing between projects requires comparing the full buyer proposition, not one headline feature. Set handover expectations, construction stage and payment schedules side by side to understand when cash is required and when use may begin.
items.question: How do I choose between projects?

items.answer: Two projects should be compared on the factors that can actually change the outcome. Review layout, specification, view, amenity package and service-charge implications rather than reducing the choice to developer name or price.
items.question: How do I compare two projects?

items.answer: Live availability can only be confirmed from a current sales or inventory source. Use a recent timestamp and identifiable source because inventory can change faster than most other project information.
items.question: How can I verify current availability?

items.answer: A developer check should focus on evidence of delivery, execution and accountability. Repeated delays, unresolved defects or weak execution create doubts about current commitments. Use official project records and completed developments rather than relying only on marketing reputation.
